clue.text: Property of a judge that's missing in Lords?

definitions.text: Property of a judge that's missing in Lords?

blocks.note: surface reading: a quality of the bench, or a judge's belongings
setter's reading: the two similes, sober as a judge and drunk as a lord

explanation.surface: A puzzle about some quality judges have that the House of Lords lacks.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue rests on two English similes: 'sober as a judge' and 'drunk as a lord'. What the judge has, the lord lacks: SOBRIETY.
explanation.definitionFit: Sobriety is the state of being sober, the trait proverbially credited to judges and denied to peers.

clue.text: One supporting group trying to find aliens

indicators.note: in a down answer, a supporting piece sits beneath and so comes last

blocks.note: a set is a group
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A member of a team searching for extraterrestrials.
explanation.walkthrough: SETI stands for the Search for Extraterrestrial Intelligence, the radio-telescope project.
explanation.definitionFit: The SETI programme scans the skies for signals from intelligent life beyond Earth.

clue.text: Try party beat

blocks.note: first meaning: an attempt, as in have a go
second meaning: to strike hard

explanation.surface: Someone trying to beat a party.
explanation.walkthrough: Really a triple definition: 'party' is a third meaning too, as a bash is a celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: To have a bash is to make an attempt, and to bash something is to hit it violently.

clue.text: Work to be done to make home on carrier

indicators.note: in a down clue the first item sits on top of the second

blocks.note: at home means in
a tray carries cups and plates

explanation.surface: A sailor being told what jobs await on an aircraft carrier.
explanation.definitionFit: An in-tray holds incoming papers awaiting attention, the office's pile of unfinished business.

clue.text: Fantastic notice on debut — and there's more to come

indicators.note: something fantastic is fanciful and unreal, so the letters are freely reimagined

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A rave review for a first night, with a promise of a sequel.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase closes a serial episode, telling the audience that the story carries on next time.

clue.text: Cheers on queen after order demanding silence

definitions.note: the answer is a noun, the code that demands silence

indicators.note: in an across clue 'on' places the first item to follow the second, tacked onto its end
placed after means the royal abbreviation is sent second, behind the honour

blocks.note: OM is the Order of Merit
ER, Elizabeth Regina
ta is British informal thanks

explanation.surface: A toast raised to the monarch after an honour is bestowed, with a call for quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is a casual British 'thanks'; the queen comes after the order, and the cheers sit on the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Omerta is the Mafia code of silence, a rule forbidding members to talk to police.

clue.text: How fellows talk openly of a marking system excluding females

blocks.note: first meaning: frankly, as between equals
second meaning: the defensive scheme in football or basketball, with a joke that only men are involved

explanation.walkthrough: In sport, each defender marks one opponent; 'excluding females' is a playful nod to the word man.
explanation.definitionFit: Man-to-man describes candid conversation and also a defensive tactic where each player guards a single opponent.

clue.text: Where merry men gathered to play with each other

blocks.note: first meaning: the outlaws of Sherwood Forest clustered about their leader
second meaning: a tournament where every competitor meets every other

explanation.walkthrough: The Merry Men were Robin Hood's band, so they gathered 'round Robin'.
explanation.definitionFit: A round robin is a competition format in which each entrant plays all the others in turn.

clue.text: Last buyers getting treated in an unusual way

indicators.note: treated letters are processed and altered into a new order

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: The final customers of the day receiving odd service.
explanation.definitionFit: Abstrusely means in an obscure, hard-to-grasp manner, out of the ordinary run of understanding.

clue.text: Lab equipment containers tossed into river

blocks.note: the Test is a river in Hampshire, England
tubes hold toothpaste, paint and the like

explanation.surface: Someone throwing containers into a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Test is a chalk stream in Hampshire, famous for trout fishing; the containers are dropped onto the end of the river.
explanation.definitionFit: Test tubes are the narrow glass vessels used in every chemistry laboratory for holding samples.

clue.text: Dirty joke perhaps is the last thing a bride needs

definitions.text: the last thing a bride needs

blocks.note: first meaning: a risque item, since blue means smutty

blocks.clueFragment: the last thing a bride needs
blocks.note: second meaning: the final item in the wedding rhyme

explanation.walkthrough: The rhyme runs 'something old, something new, something borrowed, something blue'. 'The last thing a bride needs' sounds like something unwanted, but means final in the list.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue humour is crude, and the wedding custom ends with a blue token for the bride to wear.

clue.text: Poles picked up sound contents in parts of speech

indicators.note: the contents of a word are what sits inside it, its first and last letters stripped
the two poles pick up, that is take in, something between them

blocks.note: N and S, the north and south poles
the inside letters of the word sound

explanation.surface: Eastern Europeans hearing grammatical content.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Picked up sound' suggests a homophone, but nothing is spoken: the poles pick up the inside of 'sound'.
explanation.definitionFit: Nouns are one category in grammar's classification of words, alongside verbs and adjectives.

clue.text: Expanded drying material extracted from metal casing

indicators.note: something extracted from a phrase is pulled out of it, the surrounding letters discarded

blocks.note: the run of letters across the two words, with the outer ones dropped
the short name written out in full

explanation.surface: A desiccant pulled out of a metal container.
explanation.walkthrough: The hidden word is only the short form; 'Expanded' asks for its full two-word name.
explanation.definitionFit: Talcum powder absorbs moisture from skin after washing, so it is a drying agent.

clue.text: Medical direction not to swallow?

blocks.note: surface reading: a doctor's order about pills
setter's reading: the hospital sign forbidding a patient any food or drink

explanation.surface: A doctor telling a patient not to gulp something down.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that this is close to literal: the notice above a hospital bed means nothing at all may be taken orally.
explanation.definitionFit: Nil by mouth is the hospital instruction that a patient receive no food or fluids orally.

clue.text: Comedian running school in settlers' caravan

blocks.note: a wag is a joker
a show that is on is running
to school is to train

explanation.surface: A comic operating a school among pioneers on the move.
explanation.walkthrough: 'School' is a verb here, not a building.
explanation.definitionFit: A wagon train was a convoy of covered wagons carrying pioneers across the American West.

clue.text: Country wit visited by artist

indicators.note: a place visited by someone has that person inside it

blocks.note: intelligence quotient, a measure of one's wits
Royal Academician

explanation.surface: A clever person receiving a painter as a guest.
explanation.definitionFit: Iraq is a nation in the Middle East, with Baghdad as its capital city.

clue.text: Lacking leader, Britain is to run riot — for starters

indicators.note: without its leader the following word loses its opening letter
letters running riot are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: the country's name without its first letter
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A headline warning of rioting in leaderless Britain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For starters' reads like a phrase meaning 'to begin with', but 'for' is a link and 'starters' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Initiators are people who set things going, so they are the starters of an action or process.

clue.text: Cosy tale about apostles

indicators.note: turned about, the letters are moved around into another order

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A comfortable story about Jesus's followers.
explanation.definitionFit: Acolytes are devoted followers or assistants, and apostles in the looser sense are committed disciples.

clue.text: Disease creates strange itch on ribs

indicators.note: a strange version of the words is an odd rearrangement of their letters

blocks.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: An illness showing up as an odd itch across the ribcage.
explanation.definitionFit: Bronchitis is an inflammation of the airways in the lungs, a common respiratory illness.

clue.text: She wastes every second in larking around

indicators.note: throwing away each second letter leaves only the odd ones
turned around, the kept letters run backwards

blocks.note: the first, third, fifth and seventh letters

explanation.surface: A woman frittering away time while fooling about.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl is a young female, so the pronoun she can stand for one.

clue.text: SF writer announced when I'm leaving

indicators.note: something announced is spoken out, so we go by the sound

blocks.note: when becomes as, and leaving becomes moving off

explanation.surface: A science-fiction author declaring his departure.
explanation.walkthrough: Isaac Asimov wrote the Foundation and robot stories.
explanation.definitionFit: Asimov was a prolific American author of science fiction, SF being the usual abbreviation.

clue.text: Expert in dealing with gold and silver, perhaps

definitions.text: Expert in dealing with gold and silver, perhaps

blocks.clueFragment: Expert in dealing with gold and silver
blocks.note: surface reading: a bullion trader or precious-metals dealer
setter's reading: dealing with them as materials, studying how metals behave

explanation.surface: A specialist trader in precious metals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dealing' suggests buying and selling; here it means handling scientifically, and gold and silver are just examples of metals.
explanation.definitionFit: A metallurgist is a scientist who studies the properties and processing of metals such as gold and silver.

clue.text: Boss that is missing when responsibilities are brought up

indicators.note: when something is missing it has been taken out of the word
in a down clue, bringing up means reading from bottom to top

blocks.note: i.e., Latin id est
duties are responsibilities

explanation.surface: A manager absent when duties are raised in a meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boss' suggests a manager; here it is a raised knob or stud on a surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A boss is a round ornamental knob, and a stud is a similar projecting nail head or knob.

clue.text: Russian state's vice president asked to reply in French, initially

indicators.note: taken initially means only the opening letter of each word is used

blocks.note: the opening letters of these four words

explanation.surface: A Russian deputy leader invited to respond in French.
explanation.walkthrough: RSVP stands for French 'répondez s'il vous plaît', please reply, printed on invitations.
explanation.definitionFit: Written on an invitation, the abbreviation requests an answer, coming from a French phrase.

clue.text: Essentially, clunky chapter is not suitable

indicators.note: the essence of each word is its core, its outer letters peeled away

blocks.note: the core of the word with two letters off each end
the core of the word with two letters off each end

explanation.surface: A critic judging a badly written chapter unfit for print.
explanation.definitionFit: Unapt is an uncommon form of inapt, meaning inappropriate or not fitting the purpose.

clue.text: Exclude benefits outside European range

indicators.note: one word sits outside the other, wrapping around it

blocks.note: the dole is British unemployment benefit
to omit is to leave out

explanation.surface: An instruction to strip benefits from people outside Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: The dole is the British name for state unemployment pay.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dolomites are a mountain range in north-eastern Italy, part of the Southern Alps.

clue.text: On the ground, holding small upright

indicators.note: the phrase holds a letter, taking it in among its own
something ground is crushed and broken up, so its letters are reshuffled

blocks.note: taken as written
S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: Something lying on the earth with a little thing standing up in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the ground' reads as a single location phrase, but 'ground' is the anagram signal for the two words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: An upright person is morally straight and truthful, which is what honest describes.

clue.text: Duke happy after suit delivered

indicators.note: placed after means these pieces follow the next word in the answer

blocks.note: to suit or serve a purpose
D is the abbreviation for duke
up as in cheerful, in an up mood

explanation.surface: An aristocrat cheered once his tailored suit arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suit' looks like clothing; here it is the verb, to suit a purpose.
explanation.definitionFit: Served up means presented or handed over, as a meal or a result is delivered.
